      "observations": [
        "Parent/root read all 1263 owned full-show lines across 26 paths. Graph gets its own registered outgoing constructor instead of sharing the EWS constructor. Generic account-test setup, server factory definitions, mock request dispatch, Rust sending and generated metadata change together. Cargo.lock and generated files are owned functional output, not a bulk exclusion.",
        "The original send operation checks on_send_start, base64-encodes the RFC822 string, creates a draft, extracts its ID and sends that draft. DSN and Bcc parameters are explicitly stored in underscore-prefixed unused fields. The original method does not update those properties, implement a cleanup request after later failure or prove delivery. The shared start return still means a detached operation began, not a completed send.",
        "Fixed accepted code adds a PATCH with is_delivery_receipt_requested and Bcc recipients between draft creation and send. It uses a separate create helper and later operation-request/security options. Those are later phases, not features of this original two-request landing. The accepted Rustdoc still names creation and send; the actual code also contains the intervening update. No Graph service behavior or failure rollback was executed.",
        "The generator dispatch changes from a hard-coded GET/PATCH/POST switch to request-body presence. The selected method comes from operation.method, allowing the new bodyless POST /send and generated DELETE folder operation. A generated operation is not evidence that a high-level folder-delete feature was wired or tested. The new delta assertion has a nonempty constraint message; missing should alone is not a review defect.",
        "The original generic send_request converts a zero-byte body to JSON null before typed parsing, allowing its unit-response path without parsing an empty byte slice. Accepted code keeps that conversion in send_request_json_response, while current send_request returns a raw Response and modern sending uses that path for update/send. Do not attribute current response-layer separation to this original or assume every response type accepts null.",
        "The original fake Graph server decodes the draft request, stores its payload by ID and returns202 for a known send ID or404 otherwise, setting lastSentMessage on success. Current mock retains that observable outcome through a GraphMessage object. Network identity aliases do not mean the fake HTTP server listens on the aliased port. Shared server definitions use Graph at virtual test.test:8080 to avoid the EWS port.",
        "Three new Graph task wrappers reuse existing toolbar, File menu and accelerator-key helpers. Bounded accepted helpers directly assert button/menu availability, prompt preference transitions and a generated Subject substring in lastSentMessage after the compose window closes. The File-menu task has the explicit macosx skip. No new assertion site is added; inherited prompt labels dialog text/dialog buttons are nonempty but do not state the expected behavior and predate this landing. No live keyboard/accessibility run occurred.",
        "The changed test head creates protocol-specific account/identity/outgoing objects through a generic helper, disables FCC, and returns role-specific Graph/EWS aliases. Original code uses nsIEwsServer.initialize and /v1.0; fixed accepted setup uses IExchangeOutgoingServer.exchangeUrl and a base URL. Preserve those API phases. Initial resource creation precedes the file cleanup registration; this writing-rule observation does not become an unrelated patch defect.",
        "The public send Rustdoc is rewritten to name Graph creation/send endpoints instead of copying the EWS CreateItem term. The submitted one-word EWS-to-Graph replacement is not the complete adopted text. Parameter names, async ownership, method/body dispatch, source/test roles, control grouping and assertions were inspected manually. No source, instruction, helper or generated file was edited; no Rust/Graph/compose/SSL/build/test run occurred.",
        "The complete shared primary2008856 original was read once by B for both parts and retained under its original identity/time. This second part wires the actual Graph constructor and send path; first-part genericization alone is not credited with Graph transport. Related2008857 and dependencies2012730/2011671/2011672 are locators, not newly audited bodies.",
        "C read D288895 creation-to-final timeline and four actual inline bodies, including the literal copied-comment replacement. Parent read those exact retained bodies and compared the actual source. Reviewer suggests EWS-to-Graph wording, but author notes that CreateItem is also EWS-specific and rewrites the Rustdoc to name message creation/send requests. Done alone is not adoption proof.",
        "The author explicitly defers Bcc/DSN because generated types could not then be instantiated for updates, and removes unused SSL test definitions because certificate-error handling was unavailable at that stage. The original unused fields and only-plain server definition are source facts; the reason is an attributed historical report. Fixed accepted DSN/Bcc and transport behavior are later phases, not evidence that this landing already supported them.",
        "The generator merge-conflict warning is prospective and Not Done, not an executed conflict or a global rule. Earlier rustfmt failures, later completed remote builds and the Try link are historical reports. The public-method endpoint documentation preference is scoped author opinion. No Graph, SSL, compose, generator or native test was executed."
